sentences.text: In an accident that occurred on 17.05.2015 between a motorcycle and a Maruti Alto car, the claimant, who was a pillion rider suffered grievous injuries, for which, he preferred a claim petition.

2. The Tribunal initially assessed the evidence and came to the conclusion that the accident did occur and the claimant had suffered 15% disability to the whole body and proceeded to award a sum of Rs.6,96,776/-.

3. Subsequently, the claimant preferred a review petition before the Tribunal and the Tribunal proceeded to review its order and came to the conclusion that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 55%, in addition to 15% disability and, therefore, compensation has to be enhanced by a further sum of Rs.6,00,600/- in addition to NC: 2024:KHC:51067 Rs.1,63,800/- i.e.,
Rs.7,64,400/- towards loss of future income.
4. Being aggrieved by this, both the insurer as well as the claimant are in appeal.
5. The insurer basically contends that the Tribunal could not have entertained the review petition and re- appreciated the entire evidence.

It also contends that if the claimant was aggrieved by the extent of disability assessed by the Tribunal or the amount of compensation determined by the Tribunal, he ought to have preferred an appeal and remedy of review could not have been invoked to seek enhancement of compensation.
6.
The claimant, on the other hand, contends that there was glaring error which was apparent on the face of the record and the remedy of review was therefore resorted to.
He also submits that the sums awarded were inadequate.

As far as the argument of the insurer is concerned, though it cannot be in doubt that the Tribunal in exercise of powers of review under Order XLVII Rule 1 read with Section 151 of CPC cannot basically re- appreciate the evidence and come to the conclusion that the extent of disability or the amount awarded was inadequate.

Nevertheless, it is to be noticed that the Tribunals are entrusted with the job of awarding just compensation and if in the given case the Tribunal was of the view that there was an error which was apparent on the face of the record, the Tribunal can exercise the power of review.
Be that as it may, since the matter is now before this Court, the manner of determination of compensation will have to be re-looked.
8. In this case, the evidence on record indicates that the claimant had suffered fracture of both bones of his right leg and also fracture of shaft of left humerus.
The Orthopedic Surgeon, who was NC: 2024:KHC:51067 examined, had stated that the claimant had suffered 45% permanent disability to the limb.

Apart from the said evidence, the claimant also adduced the evidence of Dr.Vasan, who was a Neurosurgeon, who had opined that the claimant had problems in balancing himself while walking and standing and he had also opined that the claimant had disability of 30%
in respect of ataxia and 25% in respect of intellectual impairment and thus, the claimant had suffered 55% total permanent disability to the whole body.

sentences.text:
In my view, in light of assessment of disability of the claimant by the Orthopedic Surgeon to an extent of 45% permanent disability to the limb and in light of assessment of disability by the Neurosurgeon that the claimant had intellectual impairment of 25% and disability of ataxia at 30%,
which stands subsequent to the assessment by the Orthopedic Surgeon and which also states that the claimant had difficulty in NC: 2024:KHC:51067 walking and standing and that he needs an attendant every time to go out due to his unsteadiness, in my view, it would be appropriate to assess the whole body disability of the claimant at 55%.
10. The Tribunal has determined the notional income of the claimant at Rs.7,000/- since there was no proof of actual income.

In such circumstances, it would be appropriate to adopt the notional income determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which for the accident of the year 2015 would be Rs.9,000/-.
11.

Since the claimant suffered disability in excess of 20% and was aged 48 years as per driving licence - Ex.P.13, 25% requires to be added towards future prospects, which makes his income to be Rs.11,250/- (Rs.9,000/- + 25%).

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.9,65,250/-
(Rs.11,250/- X 12 X 13 multiplier X 55%).

In view of the disability suffered by the claimant, it would be appropriate to enhance Rs.50,000/- awarded towards 'pain and sufferings' to Rs.1,00,000/-, and Rs.20,000/- awarded towards 'loss of amenities' to Rs.1,00,000/-.
13. As per the evidence on record, since the claimant was hospitalized for 24 days, it would be appropriate to award Rs.25,000/- as against Rs.15,000/- towards food, attendant charges etc.

and it would also be appropriate to treat the laid up period as 4 months and consequently, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.36,000/- (Rs.9,000/- X 4 months) towards loss of income during laid up period as against Rs.21,000/-.

14. The sum of Rs.3,81,976/- awarded towards 'medical expenses', and the sum of Rs.45,000/-
awarded towards future medical expenses, being based on documentary evidence, are affirmed.
15. Thus, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:
